newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's maverick singer Fela dies of AIDS.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's maverick singer Fela dies of AIDS.

text.p: Nigeria's maverick musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti, who popularised the Afro-music beat globally, has died of AIDS, his elder brother said on Sunday.

"The immediate cause of death of Fela was heart failure but there were many complications arising from the Acquired Immuno-Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS)", Olikoye Ransome-Kuti, a medical doctor, told a news conference.
The singer, composer and saxophonist, who was 58 and known to his fans simply as Fela, died on Saturday after several weeks of illness.
Funeral arrangements were not immediately announced.
Hundreds of tearful people gathered at "The Shrine", Fela's home and club in the Ikeja working class district of Lagos, the commercial capital, to mourn their idol.
Despite his outrageous lifestyle of openly smoking marijuana, dressing in his underpants and sleeping with large number of women, Fela was still a legend among his teeming fans.
AIDS is becoming increasingly common in impoverished Nigeria, Africa's most populous of 100 million people.
But there is yet to be an official and accurate medical figure for the number of AIDS-infected patients in Nigeria.

For decades, Fela who refused treatment by both Western and traditional doctors when he was ill, remained a thorn to military governments that ruled Nigeria -- a cause for which he was detained several times and even imprisoned on a variety of charges.

Earlier this year, he was held by the drugs squad which said it hoped to reform his character and turn him away from smoking marijuana -- but the narcotics agents later released him, admitting defeat.

In his final two years, Fela made no effort to oppose military ruler General Sani Abacha, even though one of his brothers, democracy activist Beko Ransome-Kuti, is serving a prison term for involvement in an alleged coup plot.
Fela stayed at home mostly at his Ikeja home and gave infrequent, and usually brief, musical performances at The Shrine.
During his heyday, Fela changed part of the family name from Ransome to Anikulapo -- which means "one who keeps death in his pouch" in his local Yoruba language.
